channel.title: QuotePlace — Quote of the Day
channel.description: One quote, every day, chosen deterministically from the QuotePlace collection.

item.title: Mary Shelley — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-10
item.description: “I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed.” — Mary Shelley

item.title: Rudyard Kipling — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-09
item.description: “I keep six honest serving-men (They taught me all I knew); their names are What and Why and When and How and Where and Who.” — Rudyard Kipling

item.title: Clive James — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-08
item.description: “It's only when you look at an ant through a magnifying glass on a sunny day that you realise how often they burst into flames.” — Clive James

item.title: Rumi — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-07
item.description: “When I am silent, I have thunder hidden inside.” — Rumi

item.title: Sri Aurobindo — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-06
item.description: “All problems of existence are essentially problems of harmony.” — Sri Aurobindo

item.title: Aristotle — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-05
item.description: “All men by nature desire to know.” — Aristotle

item.title: Kahlil Gibran — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-04
item.description: “A little knowledge that acts is worth infinitely more than much knowledge that is idle.” — Kahlil Gibran

item.title: Pablo Picasso — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-03
item.description: “Every act of creation is first an act of destruction.” — Pablo Picasso
